before.html:
Question 1
?

Solve the initial value problem x′(t)=[1003]x(t),x(0)=[−11].

a
x(t)=[−10]et+[01]e3t
b
x(t)=[01]e3t
c
x(t)=[10]et+[01]e3t
d
x(t)=[−10]et
e
 x(t)=[−10]et+[0−1]e3t
Submit

decision.explanation: The system decouples into x₁′=x₁ and x₂′=3x₂. The initial values give x₁(t)=-e^t and x₂(t)=e^{3t}, so option a satisfies both the differential equation and the initial condition.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
We have a decoupled system. Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Now, we need to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial condition $x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =-1\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+1\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 1
?

Solve the initial value problem x′(t)=[1003]x(t),x(0)=[−11].

a
x(t)=[−10]et+[01]e3t
b
x(t)=[01]e3t
c
x(t)=[10]et+[01]e3t
d
x(t)=[−10]et
e
 x(t)=[−10]et+[0−1]e3t
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We have a decoupled system. Therefore, the general solution is given by

x(t)=c1[10]et+c2[01]e3t,c1,c2∈R.

Now, we need to find the values of c1 and c2 using the initial condition x(0)=[−11]. Substituting t=0 into the general solution gives

x(0)=c1[10]+c2[01][−11]=[c1c2].

Therefore, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

x(t)=−1⋅[10]et+1⋅[01]e3t=[−10]et+[01]e3t.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms c₁=-1 and c₂=1, giving x(t)=(-e^t,e^{3t})ᵀ, which is option a. Its derivative equals diag(1,3)x(t), and x(0)=(-1,1)ᵀ. Option c fails the initial condition because its first component at t=0 is 1.

content.knowledge_point: Solving an Initial Value Problem for a Decoupled Linear System of First-Order ODEs
content.worked_solution:
We have a decoupled system. Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Now, we need to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial condition $x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =-1\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+1\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}.\end{aligned}
$$

a
x(t)=c1[01]e3πt,c1∈R
b
x(t)=c1[10]e−3t+c2[01]eπt,c1,c2∈R
c
x(t)=c1[10]e−πt+c2[01]e3t,c1,c2∈R

decision.explanation: Each equation solves independently: x₁(t)=c₁e^{-3t} and x₂(t)=c₂e^{πt}. Their two arbitrary constants give the general solution in option b.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Find the general solution to the system of differential equations
${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=-3{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=\pi {x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}$
after.worked_solution:
Given a decoupled system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 \\ 0 & {\lambda }_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}],
$$

the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

First, we write our differential equation in matrix form:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & \pi \end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

Since the matrix of the differential system is diagonal, the system is decoupled. 

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{\pi t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Question 2
?

Find the general solution to the system of differential equations {x1′(t)=−3x1(t)x2′(t)=πx2(t).

a
x(t)=c1[01]e3πt,c1∈R
b
x(t)=c1[10]e−3t+c2[01]eπt,c1,c2∈R
c
x(t)=c1[10]e−πt+c2[01]e3t,c1,c2∈R
d
x(t)=c1[10]e−3πt,c1∈R
e
x(t)=c1[10]e3πt+c2[01]e−πt,c1,c2∈R
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Given a decoupled system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

[x1′(t)x2′(t)]=[λ100λ2][x1(t)x2(t)], the formula for the general solution is x(t)=c1[10]eλ1t+c2[01]eλ2t,c1,c2∈R.

First, we write our differential equation in matrix form:

[x1′(t)x2′(t)]=[−300π][x1(t)x2(t)]

Since the matrix of the differential system is diagonal, the system is decoupled.

Therefore, the general solution is given by

x(t)=c1[10]e−3t+c2[01]eπt,c1,c2∈R.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to a Decoupled Linear System of Differential Equations
content.problem:
Find the general solution to the system of differential equations
${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=-3{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=\pi {x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}$
content.worked_solution:
Given a decoupled system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 \\ 0 & {\lambda }_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}],
$$

the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

First, we write our differential equation in matrix form:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & \pi \end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

Since the matrix of the differential system is diagonal, the system is decoupled. 

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{\pi t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Find the general solution to the system of differential equations {x1′(t)=ex1(t)x2′(t)=−2x2(t).

a
x(t)=c1[10]eet+c2[01]e−2t,c1,c2∈R
b
x(t)=c1[10]et+c2[01]e−2t,c1,c2∈R
c
x(t)=c1[10]e−2t+c2[01]et,c1,c2∈R
d
x(t)=c1[10]eet+c2[01]e2t,c1,c2∈R
e

decision.explanation: For x′=λx, the general solution is ce^{λt}. Thus x₁(t)=c₁e^{et} and x₂(t)=c₂e^{-2t}, with independent arbitrary constants, matching option a.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Find the general solution to the system of differential equations
${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=e{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-2{x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}$
after.worked_solution:
Given a decoupled system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 \\ 0 & {\lambda }_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}],
$$

the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

First, we write our differential equation in matrix form:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}e & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

Since the matrix of the differential system is diagonal, the system is decoupled. 

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{et}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Question 3
?

Find the general solution to the system of differential equations {x1′(t)=ex1(t)x2′(t)=−2x2(t).

a
x(t)=c1[10]eet+c2[01]e−2t,c1,c2∈R
b
x(t)=c1[10]et+c2[01]e−2t,c1,c2∈R
c
x(t)=c1[10]e−2t+c2[01]et,c1,c2∈R
d
x(t)=c1[10]eet+c2[01]e2t,c1,c2∈R
e
x(t)=c1[10]e2t+c2[01]e−et,c1,c2∈R
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Given a decoupled system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

[x1′(t)x2′(t)]=[λ100λ2][x1(t)x2(t)], the formula for the general solution is x(t)=c1[10]eλ1t+c2[01]eλ2t,c1,c2∈R.

First, we write our differential equation in matrix form:

[x1′(t)x2′(t)]=[e00−2][x1(t)x2(t)]

Since the matrix of the differential system is diagonal, the system is decoupled.

Therefore, the general solution is given by

x(t)=c1[10]eet+c2[01]e−2t,c1,c2∈R.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option a. Differentiating x₁=c₁e^{et} gives x₁′=ex₁, and differentiating x₂=c₂e^{-2t} gives x₂′=-2x₂. The two arbitrary constants cover all solutions. Option b instead gives x₁′=x₁ and fails the first equation in general.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to a Decoupled Linear System of Differential Equations
content.problem:
Find the general solution to the system of differential equations
${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=e{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-2{x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}$
content.worked_solution:
Given a decoupled system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 \\ 0 & {\lambda }_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}],
$$

the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

First, we write our differential equation in matrix form:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}e & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

Since the matrix of the differential system is diagonal, the system is decoupled. 

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{et}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Question 4
?

Find the general solution to the system of differential equations {x1′(t)=0x2′(t)=ln⁡(2)x2(t).

a
x(t)=c1[10]+c2[01]2et,c1,c2∈R
b
x(t)=c2[01]2t,c1,c2∈R
c
x(t)=c2[01]e2t,c1,c2∈R
d
x(t)=c1[10]+c2[01]2t,c1,c2∈R
e
x(t)=c1[10]et+c2[01]2t,c1,c2∈R
Submit

decision.explanation: The first equation gives x₁(t)=c₁. The second gives x₂(t)=c₂e^{ln(2)t}=c₂2^t. Both constants are arbitrary, so option d is the general solution. Option b omits solutions with nonzero first component.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Find the general solution to the system of differential equations
${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=0 \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2){x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}$
after.worked_solution:
Given a decoupled system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 \\ 0 & {\lambda }_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}],
$$

the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

First, we write our differential equation in matrix form:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & \operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

Since the matrix of the differential system is diagonal, the system is decoupled. 

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{2}^{t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to a Decoupled Linear System of Differential Equations
content.problem:
Find the general solution to the system of differential equations
${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=0 \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2){x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}$
content.worked_solution:
Given a decoupled system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 \\ 0 & {\lambda }_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}],
$$

the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

First, we write our differential equation in matrix form:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & \operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

Since the matrix of the differential system is diagonal, the system is decoupled. 

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{2}^{t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Solve the initial value problem x′(t)=[−ln⁡2007]x(t),x(0)=[9−5].

a
x(t)=[0−5]e7t
b
x(t)=[−90]2−t+[05]7t/2
c
x(t)=[90]e−2t
d
x(t)=[0−5]e−2t+[90]e7t
e
x(t)=[90]2−t+[0−5]e7t
Submit

decision.explanation: The decoupled equations and initial values give x₁(t)=9e^{-ln(2)t}=9·2^{-t} and x₂(t)=-5e^{√7t}. This is option e and satisfies both the system and x(0)=(9,-5)ᵀ.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
We have a decoupled system. Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{\sqrt{7}t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{2}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{\sqrt{7}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial condition $x(0)=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -5\end{aligned}].$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}9 \\ -5\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =9\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{2}^{-t}+(-5)\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{\sqrt{7}t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{2}^{-t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -5\end{aligned}]{e}^{\sqrt{7}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5

Solve the initial value problem x′(t)=[−ln⁡2007]x(t),x(0)=[9−5].

a
x(t)=[0−5]e7t
b
x(t)=[−90]2−t+[05]7t/2
c
x(t)=[90]e−2t
d
x(t)=[0−5]e−2t+[90]e7t
e
x(t)=[90]2−t+[0−5]e7t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We have a decoupled system. Therefore, the general solution is given by

x(t)=c1[10]e−ln⁡2t+c2[01]e7t=c1[10]2−t+c2[01]e7t,c1,c2∈R

Now, we need to find the values of c1 and c2 using the initial condition x(0)=[9−5]. Substituting t=0 into the general solution gives

x(0)=c1[10]+c2[01][9−5]=[c1c2].

Therefore, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

x(t)=9⋅[10]2−t+(−5)⋅[01]e7t=[90]2−t+[0−5]e7t.

content.worked_solution:
We have a decoupled system. Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{\sqrt{7}t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{2}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{\sqrt{7}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial condition $x(0)=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -5\end{aligned}].$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}9 \\ -5\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =9\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{2}^{-t}+(-5)\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{\sqrt{7}t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{2}^{-t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -5\end{aligned}]{e}^{\sqrt{7}t}.\end{aligned}
$$
